what: Equifax is a credit bureau. It holds credit histories on hundreds of millions of people and sells reports and scores to lenders, and through The Work Number it also holds employment and income records used to verify applicants.
customers: Banks, card issuers, mortgage lenders, employers, landlords and government agencies.
money: income and employment verification through The Work Number
credit bureaus outside the United States
moat: Payroll records contributed directly by employers, a database no competitor can assemble, which makes verification instant rather than manual.
risks: Mortgage lending volumes drive a large part of demand and have been depressed
The 2017 data breach cost it heavily and data security remains the central risk
Debt of about $5.2 billion against almost no cash
Regulators have scrutinised credit bureau pricing and accuracy
opportunities: A recovery in mortgage lending would lift the most profitable volumes
The Work Number keeps adding employer records, widening its advantage
watch: Workforce Solutions revenue growth and mortgage inquiry volumes.
